# ics-calendar-toolkit

> Build, read and validate `.ics` calendar feeds, and keep subscribers from being notified about events that haven't changed. ESM only, Node >= 24, one runtime dependency (`ical.js`). Everything is a named export of `ics-calendar-toolkit`.

## Mental model

1. Your source rows become `CalendarEvent` objects.
2. `trackSequences` decides each event's `sequence` and `lastModified` from stored state, so only really-changed events look updated.
3. `buildFeed` writes the `.ics` text. Broken events are left out and reported in `invalid`; it does not throw on bad event data.
4. `icsValidator.validate` checks the finished text before you publish it.

## Types

- `CalendarEvent`: `{ uid, time, summary, location: string | null, geo: { lat, lon } | null, categories: string[], description: string, url, status?: 'CONFIRMED' | 'TENTATIVE' | 'CANCELLED', sequence: number, lastModified: string }`
- `EventTime`: `{ allDay: false, start, end }` with local date-times like `2026-11-15T18:30:00`, or `{ allDay: true, start, end }` with dates like `2026-11-20`. For all-day events `end` is the day AFTER the last day.
- `lastModified`: UTC ISO string, e.g. `2026-11-01T09:00:00.000Z`.
- `CalendarHeader`: `{ prodId, name, description?, refreshInterval (ISO 8601 duration, e.g. 'PT6H'), timeZone: { id, definition: string[] } }`. `definition` is your own `BEGIN:VTIMEZONE ... END:VTIMEZONE` lines, written verbatim; the toolkit does not generate them. See `examples/zone.ts` in the repository for Europe/Berlin.

## Functions

- `buildFeed(events, { header, maxTextLength, render? }) => { ics, included, invalid }`
  `invalid` is `{ uid, reason }[]`. Events are sorted by start, then UID. Output is byte-stable: same input, same bytes.
- `trackSequences({ identities, items: Map<uid, T>, options: { runDate, nowIso, keepIdentityDays, hash: (item: T) => string } }) => { entries, counts: { added, updated, removed }, identities }`
  Pass the previous run's `identities` (a `Record<uid, Identity>`; persist as JSON). Unchanged hash keeps `sequence`/`lastModified`; changed hash bumps `sequence` once; new items start at 0; UIDs unseen for `keepIdentityDays` are forgotten. Pure function, no I/O.
- `isShrunk({ previous, current, options: { massDisappearanceRatio, massDisappearanceMinEvents } }) => boolean`
  True when the event count fell sharply. Use it to refuse publishing a feed built from a broken source.
- `icsValidator.validate(ics: string | Uint8Array, expectedEvents?: number) => { ok, errors: string[], events, checks: string[] }`
  Never throws. Checks UTF-8, CRLF, line length, control characters, structure, per-event required properties, known time zones, valid dates and coordinates, unique UIDs, and an `ical.js` round trip. `new ICSValidator({ countEvents })` replaces the round-trip counter.
- `readIdentities(feedText) => { uid, sequence, lastModified }[]`
  Rebuild lost `trackSequences` state from the live feed.
- `readEvents(feedText) => CalendarEvent[]`
  Only for feeds written by this toolkit. Events lacking a property the toolkit always writes (such as `URL`) are silently skipped.
- `dropDuplicates({ records, subjectOf: (r) => { id, title, text, place, starts }, options: { titlePrefix, minTitle } }) => { kept, dropped: { record, keptInstead }[] }`
  Removes records describing the same event; first seen wins.
- Lower-level helpers: `eventLines`, `calendarText`, `escapeText`, `foldLine`, `descriptionLines`, `makeFeedBuilder`, date helpers (`addDays`, `daysBetween`, `dateOf`, `clockOf`, `icsLocal`, `icsUtc`), text helpers (`truncate`, `foldText`, `compareStrings`).

## Minimal working example

```ts
import { buildFeed, icsValidator, type CalendarEvent } from 'ics-calendar-toolkit';

const events: CalendarEvent[] = [
  {
    uid: 'meetup-1@example.org',
    time: { allDay: false, start: '2026-11-15T18:30:00', end: '2026-11-15T20:00:00' },
    summary: 'Monthly meetup',
    location: null,
    geo: null,
    categories: [],
    description: '',
    url: 'https://example.org/meetups/1',
    sequence: 0,
    lastModified: '2026-11-01T09:00:00.000Z',
  },
];

const { ics, included, invalid } = buildFeed(events, {
  header: {
    prodId: '-//example//community//EN',
    name: 'Community events',
    refreshInterval: 'PT6H',
    timeZone: { id: 'Europe/Berlin', definition: [/* VTIMEZONE lines */] },
  },
  maxTextLength: 1000,
});

const result = icsValidator.validate(ics, included.length);
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));
```

## Pitfalls

- Timed events are plain local strings in `header.timeZone`; DST gaps and overlaps are your responsibility.
- Every event must use a `timeZone` the header defines, or it lands in `invalid`.
- Changing property order or line folding would rewrite every event for every subscriber, so do not post-process `ics`.
- Always check `invalid` after `buildFeed`; a dropped event is not an exception.
